member.summary: Owns the WebBrowser ActiveX control and keeps it over the area a GTK widget occupies.
member.remarks:
The control is in-place activated into a bare child window of the GTK toplevel's HWND, because GTK 4 gives only toplevels a window handle. As with the WebView2 backend, the browser therefore paints above every GTK widget in the same window; overlapping widgets, popovers and menus do not clip it. Recorded as a Windows-only deviation in EMULATION-GAPS.md.
Everything here runs on the GTK main-loop thread, which the application enters through [STAThread] Main - the single-threaded apartment OLE in-place activation requires.

member.summary: Reaches the window handle behind a GTK 4 toplevel on Windows.
member.remarks:
GTK 4 has no child windows: only a toplevel owns an HWND, and every widget inside it is drawn rather than hosted. The Internet Explorer WebBrowser ActiveX control needs a parent HWND, so a child window is parented to the toplevel's and positioned by hand over the area the control occupies. member.name: T:Gtk.Windows.Forms.InternetExplorer.StaApartment
member.summary: A dedicated single-threaded apartment with its own message pump, used to host the WebBrowser ActiveX control when the application's GTK thread is not itself an STA.
member.remarks:
OLE in-place activation requires an STA, and the control's window has to be pumped on the thread that created it. When the GTK main loop runs on an MTA thread, this gives the control a correct home: every COM touch - instantiation, navigation, geometry, teardown - is marshalled here through , while the GTK widget is still read on the main thread and only the resulting bounds crossed over. The common case (a normal [STAThread] WinForms host) does not use this at all; the control then lives directly on the GTK thread.
The pump is a plain work queue drained on a wait handle rather than a Win32 message loop: the control's own window messages are dispatched by the thread between work items because this is a real STA, which is what OLE needs. This keeps the apartment free of a dependency on user32 message APIs.

member.name: T:Gtk.Windows.Forms.InternetExplorer.TridentDomChannel
member.summary: Drives the shared DOM bridge script inside MSHTML and reads values back out of it.
member.remarks:
The bridge script is the same one the WebKitGTK and WebView2 backends inject. Trident has no host message channel like chrome.webview.postMessage, so values are pulled rather than pushed: the script is injected with IHTMLWindow2.execScript, and a global function is then called through the window's script dispatch (IHTMLDocument2.Script), whose return value crosses back as a VARIANT. Everything runs synchronously on the STA thread the control lives on; the asynchronous signatures are kept so the backend presents the same seam as the out-of-process engines.
One consequence: the bridge's delegated DOM events are not delivered on this backend - there is no callback channel into the host without an IDocHostUIHandler.GetExternal sink. Document reads, mutations and script invocation all work; raised HtmlElement events do not. Recorded in EMULATION-GAPS.md.
